title: Deterministic throughput audit and customer signoff for Dedicated capacity
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a deterministic, reproducible throughput audit that validates Dedicated capacity against contract SLAs and produces a customer-facing signoff report. The audit bundles a load-harness (ChronoLoad), a documented benchmarking methodology, and a two-stage customer acceptance test plan. This ticket covers engineering work to instrument the harness, define pass/fail gates, and produce an automated signoff artifact consumable by Solutions and Sales.
background: Customers on Dedicated require predictable throughput guarantees for commitments. Existing load drivers are brittle between runs and lack deterministic workload seeds, making customer signoff ad-hoc. We need a repeatable pipeline that maps observed customer traffic characteristics to a reproducible test that verifies throughput + tail-latency SLOs and checks autoscaler behavior under degradation scenarios.
approach:
1) Implement ChronoLoad: a deterministic replay-and-synthesize harness that can (a) replay a trimmed trace with preserved inter-arrival distribution, (b) synthesize synthetic-scale variants using configurable load curves, and (c) record golden telemetry for later regression.
2) Standardize benchmarking methodology: fixed warmup, multiple steady-state sweeps, statistical aggregation across N runs, and explicit KV cache priming procedures.
3) Customer acceptance protocol: staging rehearsal with the customer, two-week soak on a dedicated pool with traffic-shadowing, and final signoff report including throughput envelope and degradation plan.
4) Integrate with Console dashboards and reporting APIs so customers can independently verify results.
success_criteria: ChronoLoad can playback any gzipped capture and produce identical request timing within a 5% inter-arrival distribution variance
Benchmark runs are reproducible across three independent runs with throughput variation < 7% and p99 latency variation < 10%
Automated signoff PDF generated with: workload fingerprint, throughput curve, p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate, and anomaly flags
Customer acceptance checklist executed for at least one pilot customer and signed off by Solutions and their engineering contact
tasks: Design ChronoLoad API and CLI (support seeds, scaling factor, ramp profiles)
Implement request-timing engine and deterministic RNG seed handling
Add KV cache priming mode that records then replays cache keys
Add autoscaler stress module to simulate node failures and forced scale-downs
Instrument additional metrics: token/sec, GPU_util, CUDA_mem, context-switches, queue-depth
Create benchmarking orchestration job templates (K8s/Batch) and integrate with CI
Wire test results into Console reporting and generate signoff artifact template
Run three pilot audits (internal tenants) and tune methodology
Partner with Solutions to run customer pilot and iterate on acceptance criteria
test_plan: Harness validation: run ChronoLoad on a synthetic 10k-request trace with known distribution. Verify timing variance <5%.
Warmup and steady-state: 3 minute warmup, 15 minute steady-state; repeat for 3 sweeps at increasing QPS (baseline, +25%, +50%).
Autoscaler behavior: during steady-state, trigger a simulated transient node loss and observe cascade; verify fallback policy and slope of recovery meets E2E SLA (time-to-stable-capacity < 90s).
Cache priming test: prime KV cache then rerun baseline to measure cache-hit delta and normalized token cost per request.
Tail-latency validation: collect p50/p95/p99 for each run, compute run-to-run CV, and flag regressions >10% p99 increase.
Customer acceptance: stage run with customer's representative traffic (shadowed), run soak for 48 hours, then run two deterministic audit sweeps and generate signoff report.
rollout_plan: Day 0: merge ChronoLoad and basic metrics to dedicated-staging cluster
Day 3: run internal pilot audits and collect feedback
Day 7: integrate Console reporting and signoff PDF generation
Day 10-14: run customer pilot with Solutions team and collect telemetry
After signoff: publish methodology docs, add to Dedicated onboarding checklist
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Customer traces contain PII or sensitive tokens. Mitigation: enforce redaction pipeline and default sampling; require DPO approval for raw traces.
Risk: Test harness impacts production clusters when misconfigured. Mitigation: run all heavy experiments in isolated pools, add circuit-breaker in orchestrator to halt at anomaly thresholds.
Risk: Autoscaler noise causes flapping during tests. Mitigation: introduce synthetic stabilization window and disable non-essential autoscaler signals during deterministic runs.
